newsitem.title: CHINA: China urged to release all political prisoners.
newsitem.headline: China urged to release all political prisoners.

text.p: An international human rights group on Monday called on China to release all political prisoners to mark the return of the British colony of Hong Kong to Beijing rule at midnight.

"Human Rights in China calls upon the Chinese government to mark this historic occasion by releasing all prisoners of conscience currently being held in China," the New York-based group said in a statement.

The group named Wei Jingsheng, widely regarded as the father of China's modern democracy movement, and Wang Dan, a leader of the 1989 student-led demonstrations for democracy that were crushed by the military with heavy loss of life.
Wei, 47, is serving a 14-year jail term for subversion and Wang, 27, is serving an 11-year sentence on a similar charge.

Human Rights in China, set up by a group of exiled Chinese dissidents, said rule of law, freedom of the press, democracy and human rights were values that had been fundamental to the prosperity and stability of Hong Kong.

"By releasing all prisoners of conscience...the Chinese government can demonstrate to the people of Hong Kong and the world its intention to uphold these values in Hong Kong and to move toward a political system that guarantees them throughout China," it said.

International human rights groups and Hong Kong democrats are pessimistic about the future of the territory after it reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight following 156 years of British colonial rule.
China considers jailed dissidents common criminals and rejects criticisms of its human rights record as interference in its internal affairs.
